data.note: RS-DT-JP-GREET-001 is not present in this repository (design doc SS2.2 Q2). Measurements below use the substitute Tensor training loop model (entity_migration_regression_tests/test_phase_e2_regression_performance.py), migrated per the design's SS13 table (learning rate / current step / loss).

entity_free_compile_overhead.method: Median of 10 compilations per fixture, compared against artifacts/reason_entity/f0/performance_baseline.json (Phase F0, pre-Entity baseline), same 14-fixture corpus.

ru_slot_runtime_overhead.method: Median of 15 executions of the substitute 8-step Tensor training loop, plain-let version vs ru:/derive:/<- version, same seed.

compile_overhead_entity_using_program.method: Median of 15 compilations of the same substitute training loop, plain-let version vs ru:/derive:/<- version.
compile_overhead_entity_using_program.note: No specific design target for this combination (RS-RE-FSM-001 SS9.4 only sets targets for Entity-free code and RU-Slot-using runtime execution); reported for completeness.

migration_equivalence.note: The RS-DT-JP-GREET-001-specific criterion (identical loss curve to a pre-existing external baseline checkpoint) does not apply since that model is unavailable. What was verified instead: the same Tensor training computation, written twice (plain let/reassignment vs ru:/derive:/<-), produces byte-identical tensor_trace and final result.

bug_found_during_this_phase.description: frontend.integrated_computation_runtime._statements' per-statement runtime.collect(env) call (used throughout ordinary execution, including inside while loops) was not entity-scope-aware. An Entity-held Tensor (e.g. a ru: weight = tensor.parameter(...) updated across training iterations) could be prematurely garbage-collected mid-loop, raising TSF-018 (invalid Tensor value reference).
bug_found_during_this_phase.root_cause: Phase E1 added the RUSlot-awareness fix (RS-RE-FSM-001 SS3.8/C-5) only to the two runtime.collect() call sites in execute_program(), missing the third call site inside _statements() itself -- the one that actually runs on every statement, including loop iterations.
bug_found_during_this_phase.fix: frontend/integrated_computation_runtime.py: _statements() now reads _CURRENT_ENTITY_SCOPE and passes scope.environment.all_slots() as an extra collect() root when a scope is active.
bug_found_during_this_phase.discovered_by: Migrating a real multi-step Tensor training loop to ru:/derive:/<- during Phase E2 -- exactly the kind of Tensor-heavy regression scenario this Phase exists to catch.
